items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: Johnny Mince was in the band before I got in it, but that was the band that Tommy Dorsey was to take over, Joe Haynes is a very sensitive sort of guy... But He was a marvelous talent.

ctx.x: I hope you are wrong, but anyway, so let's see who else was in the band. I don't think there

was anybody -- oh, yes, Johnny Mince was in the band before I got in it, but that was the band that Tommy Dorsey was to take over, Joe Haynes is a very sensitive sort of guy, but he used to wish that he could stand behind the band, he was so frightened of the public. But He was a marvelous talent.

Then, from that job Toots Mondello and I got an offer and Pee Wee Erwin, the three of us got an offer to go with Ray Noble. Now, as you know, Ray Noble was a fine musician who had made a lot of recordings here in England and was not allowed to bring the whole band in to the States because of some labor law condition that existed or may still exist and so he brought Al Bawly, who was a very good singer in those days -- we are not talking about jazz now, we are talking about dance bands.
